facts.title: It started in Boston
facts.fact: The franchise was founded in 1932 as the Boston Braves. Boston was awarded the team on July 9, 1932, with George Preston Marshall as owner.

facts.title: First name change
facts.fact: In 1933 the team changed its name after moving its home games to Fenway Park.

facts.title: Moving to Washington
facts.fact: The team relocated to Washington, D.C. on February 13, 1937.

facts.title: Signing Slinging Sammy
facts.fact: Washington signed TCU rookie quarterback Sammy Baugh on December 12, 1936, and built its offense around his passing.

facts.title: A title in year one
facts.fact: In its first season in Washington, the team won the 1937 NFL Championship Game over the Chicago Bears on December 12, 1937.

facts.title: The one we don't talk about
facts.fact: The Bears beat Washington 73 to 0 in the 1940 title game, the most lopsided score in NFL championship history.

facts.title: Payback
facts.fact: Two years later, Washington won the 1942 NFL Championship Game 14 to 6 over a previously undefeated Bears team.

facts.title: Lost by a safety
facts.fact: The Cleveland Rams beat Washington 15 to 14 in the 1945 title game. The deciding safety led to a rule change known as the Baugh/Marshall Rule.

facts.title: Triple crown
facts.fact: In 1943 Sammy Baugh led the league in pass completions, punting (45.9-yard average) and interceptions (11).

facts.title: A punting record for 82 years
facts.fact: Baugh averaged 51.4 yards per punt in 1940. It stood as the single-season record until 2022.

facts.title: One team, sixteen seasons
facts.fact: "Slinging Sammy" Baugh played all 16 of his NFL seasons in Washington, from 1937 to 1952. He was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1963.

facts.title: The fight song
facts.fact: Washington was among the first NFL franchises with an original fight song, played after home touchdowns since 1937.

facts.title: Griffith Stadium
facts.fact: After the move, the team played at Griffith Stadium from 1937 through 1960.

facts.title: Moving to RFK
facts.fact: Washington played at RFK Stadium from 1961 to 1996.

facts.title: Last to integrate
facts.fact: Under federal pressure, the team integrated in 1962, the last pro football franchise to do so.

facts.title: Lombardi's one season
facts.fact: Vince Lombardi coached Washington to a 7-5-2 record in 1969. He died of cancer shortly before the 1970 season.

facts.title: The first Super Bowl trip
facts.fact: George Allen, hired in January 1971, took the 1972 team to Super Bowl VII. Washington lost 14 to 7 to the undefeated Miami Dolphins.

facts.title: Enter Jack Kent Cooke
facts.fact: Jack Kent Cooke bought majority control in 1974 and became sole owner in 1985.

facts.title: Drafting Art Monk
facts.fact: Washington took Art Monk in the first round of the 1980 draft, 18th overall. He played 14 seasons for the team.

facts.title: Gibbs arrives
facts.fact: Jack Kent Cooke signed Joe Gibbs as head coach on January 13, 1981.

facts.title: Okay, you hogs
facts.fact: Offensive line coach Joe Bugel coined "The Hogs" at 1982 training camp, telling Russ Grimm and Jeff Bostic: "Okay, you hogs, let's get running down there."

facts.title: Honorary Hog
facts.fact: Running back John Riggins was accepted by the offensive line as an "Honorary Hog."

facts.title: The strike season
facts.fact: A 57-day players' strike cut the 1982 season to nine games. Washington went 8-1.

facts.title: Super Bowl XVII
facts.fact: On January 30, 1983, at the Rose Bowl, Washington beat the Miami Dolphins 27 to 17 for its first Super Bowl title.

facts.title: Fourth and one
facts.fact: In the fourth quarter, facing fourth-and-one at Miami's 43, John Riggins ran 43 yards for the touchdown that gave Washington its first lead, 20 to 17.

facts.title: Riggo's workload
facts.fact: Riggins ran for 166 yards on 38 carries in Super Bowl XVII, both Super Bowl records at the time, and was named MVP.

facts.title: Last pick of the first round
facts.fact: Darrell Green was the last player taken in the first round of the 1983 draft, 28th overall.

facts.title: 106 catches
facts.fact: Art Monk caught 106 passes in 1984, a then-NFL record.

facts.title: The fastest man
facts.fact: Darrell Green won the NFL's Fastest Man competition four times and is its only undefeated multiple winner.

facts.title: Running on torn cartilage
facts.fact: In a 1987 divisional playoff at Chicago, Green returned a punt 52 yards for the winning touchdown, 21 to 17, after tearing rib cartilage on the return.

facts.title: Super Bowl XXII
facts.fact: On January 31, 1988, in San Diego, Washington beat the Denver Broncos 42 to 10.

facts.title: 35 in one quarter
facts.fact: Washington scored 35 points in the second quarter of Super Bowl XXII: five touchdowns on 18 offensive plays.

facts.title: Doug Williams makes history
facts.fact: Doug Williams threw for 340 yards and four touchdowns, won MVP, and became the first African-American starting quarterback to win a Super Bowl.

facts.title: Timmy Smith's 204
facts.fact: Rookie Timmy Smith ran for 204 yards in Super Bowl XXII, a Super Bowl record.

facts.title: 14 and 2
facts.fact: The 1991 team went 14-2 in the regular season.

facts.title: Super Bowl XXVI
facts.fact: On January 26, 1992, at the Metrodome in Minneapolis, Washington beat the Buffalo Bills 37 to 24.

facts.title: Rypien's night
facts.fact: Mark Rypien completed 18 of 33 passes for 292 yards and two touchdowns and was named Super Bowl XXVI MVP.

facts.title: Three rings
facts.fact: The Hogs helped Washington win Super Bowls XVII, XXII and XXVI under Joe Gibbs.

facts.title: A new home
facts.fact: Since 1997 the team has played in Landover, Maryland, at the stadium now called Northwest Stadium.

facts.title: Twenty seasons
facts.fact: Darrell Green played 20 seasons, all in Washington (1983 to 2002), and set an NFL record with an interception in 19 straight seasons.

facts.title: Gibbs, part two
facts.fact: Joe Gibbs came back as head coach and team president on January 7, 2004.

facts.title: Number 21
facts.fact: Washington drafted safety Sean Taylor fifth overall in 2004 out of Miami. He died in November 2007 at age 24, and the team retired his No. 21 on October 17, 2021.

facts.title: Same day, same class
facts.fact: Art Monk and Darrell Green were both inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame on August 2, 2008.

facts.title: A Hog in Canton
facts.fact: Guard Russ Grimm, an original Hog, was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2010.

facts.title: Commanders
facts.fact: After playing as the Washington Football Team, the franchise rebranded as the Commanders in 2022.

facts.title: New ownership
facts.fact: A group led by Josh Harris bought the team for $6.05 billion. The NFL approved the sale on July 20, 2023.

facts.title: Number two overall
facts.fact: Washington drafted quarterback Jayden Daniels out of LSU second overall in 2024. He won Offensive Rookie of the Year.

facts.title: Best since '91
facts.fact: The 2024 team went 12-5, its best record since 1991, then won road playoff games at Tampa Bay (23-20) and Detroit (45-31).

facts.title: Back in the NFC title game
facts.fact: The 2024 run reached the NFC Championship Game for the first time since the 1991 season.

facts.title: Burgundy and gold
facts.fact: The team's colors are officially burgundy and gold. Five league titles: 1937, 1942, and Super Bowls XVII, XXII and XXVI.
